paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Ezra told the king, "The hand of our God is gracious to all who seek Him," and then he had to decide if he meant it (Ezra 8:22). He was ashamed to ask for soldiers, so he did something harder: he fasted and asked God for a safe road. Talking about trusting God is easy, friend. Living like it, with a fortune in silver and gold on your back, is where the faith shows up.

Notice what else Ezra did, though. He did not sit around and just pray. He searched the camp, sent a team to find Levites, weighed out every piece of treasure, and told the priests, "Guard them carefully" (Ezra 8:15-17, 25-29). Trusting God and doing the work go in the SAME direction. Ezra prayed like it all depended on God and counted like it all depended on him, and I love that.

And look how it ended. They were kept safe from "the hands of the enemies and bandits along the way," and Ezra gives God the credit again and again (Ezra 8:31). So whatever road you're on this week, baker, seek Him first, do your part, and let Him be the one who gets you there. I once thought my road ended in a dusty drawer, and it turns out His hand was on me the whole time. This story isn't over yet, so keep that oven warm.
